correctness.rationale: The inverse-square visibility radius gives the capped power expectation exactly. Completing the Gaussian square yields the closed form and derivative S_prime=(alpha/2)[(alpha-1)M-p_t(0)]. For alpha>1, the integral ratio H=M/p_t(0) solves the first-order identity 2t^2 H_prime=(t+b^2t^2-d^2)H+t(d-bt). Subtracting 1/c and applying a positive integrating factor produces a derivative with the sign of a quadratic Q(t) with exactly one positive root; endpoint signs force precisely one crossing when d<0. For d>=0, H<1/b<1/c. The subcritical alpha<=1 branch is immediate. Expanding H at t=2log(1/x)+O(1) and evaluating the Gaussian boundary density proves the asymptotic. All hypotheses, boundaries and finite-versus-infinite verification limits appear in RESULT.md. Independently programmed normal-CDF and radial quadrature diagnostics plus derivative checks passed 628 assertions in verify.py; they supplement rather than constitute the proof.

value.rationale: A finite flux-limited catalog is a motivated nonlinear selection system where increasing variance at fixed arithmetic mean may improve or worsen detection. The result supplies the sharp radial-count exponent q=2 dividing universal decline from a uniquely optimum nonzero intrinsic scatter when the mean is below the edge sensitivity, plus an exact optimizer equation and faint-source asymptotic. It distinguishes a global optimum from a qualitative Jensen-effect claim and provides a reproducible analytic baseline for selection simulation. These mathematical structural conclusions are meaningful but not field-calibrated, and no practical adjustment of real population scatter is proposed.
